dataset: Calendar facts a model with a training cutoff cannot know for next year: public holidays (UK, US, Germany, France), tax-year starts and ends (UK, US, Australia, India, Canada, Germany, France, Brazil, Poland) and daylight-saving switches (UK, Germany, France, US, Australia; Brazil has none), for 2026, 2027, 2028
licence: Per source: gov.uk — Open Government Licence v3.0; OPM and the US Code — US Government works, public domain; calendrier.api.gouv.fr — Licence Ouverte 2.0; German statutes and ministry pages — official works (§ 5 UrhG); other statutes as recorded on each block.
verificationMethod: The three machine-readable sources were fetched on `fetched` (User-Agent "databutler.dev data curation (+https://databutler.dev)", 500 ms apart) and reshaped, not edited. Everything else comes from data/calendar/manual.json, where each entry names the official page it was read from on verifiedDate and quotes the sentence; rule-based dates (Easter-relative holidays, US statutory dates, DST transitions, tax-year periods) are computed by scripts/calendar.js from the quoted rule and asserted against dates official pages publish. Entries that could not be re-verified against an official page carry `nonOfficial: true` and say why.

statute.inaugurationDay: (c) January 20 of each fourth year after 1965, Inauguration Day, is a legal public holiday for the purpose of statutes relating to pay and leave of employees ... employed in the District of Columbia, Montgomery and Prince Georges Counties in Maryland, Arlington and Fairfax Counties in Virginia, and the cities of Alexandria and Falls Church in Virginia.

personal.label: tax year
personal.statement: The UK tax year for individuals runs from 6 April to 5 April of the following year.
personal.quote: The current tax year is from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.
personal.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 ("All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated © Crown copyright")

government.label: financial year
government.statement: The UK government financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
government.quote: “Financial year” means, in relation to matters relating to the Consolidated Fund, the National Loans Fund, or moneys provided by Parliament, or to the Exchequer or to central taxes or finance, the twelve months ending with 31st March.

personal.label: tax year (calendar year)
personal.statement: The US individual tax year is the calendar year, 1 January to 31 December (a fiscal year ending in another month is possible with IRS approval).
personal.quote: Calendar year – 12 consecutive months beginning January 1 and ending December 31. Fiscal year – 12 consecutive months ending on the last day of any month except December.
personal.licence: Work of the United States Government — public domain (17 U.S.C. § 105)
personal.verification: irs.gov fetched 2026-10-04; the same page: "Generally, anyone can adopt the calendar year."

government.label: federal fiscal year
government.statement: The US federal government fiscal year runs from 1 October to 30 September and is named for the calendar year in which it ends (FY2027 = 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027).
government.quote: The fiscal year of the Treasury begins on October 1 of each year and ends on September 30 of the following year.
government.licence: Work of the United States Government — public domain (17 U.S.C. § 105)

personal.label: financial year (income year)
personal.statement: The Australian financial year runs from 1 July to 30 June; it is named for both years (2026–27).
personal.publisher: Australian Revenue Offices (the state and territory revenue offices' joint payroll-tax site)
personal.quote: financial year Each year commencing on 1 July and ending 30 June.
personal.licence: No licence statement on the page; Australian government material is generally CC BY 4.0 — not confirmed for this site.
personal.verification: payrolltax.gov.au fetched 2026-10-04. The primary statute (Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 s 995-1, "financial year means a period of 12 months beginning on 1 July") sits on legislation.gov.au, which renders only with JavaScript, and ato.gov.au answers 403 to automated fetches — neither could be read by the fetcher.

personal.label: financial year / tax year
personal.statement: India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March. From 1 April 2026 the Income Tax Act, 2025 replaces the Income Tax Act, 1961 and calls the twelve months from 1 April the 'tax year' (Tax Year 2026-27), discontinuing the 'previous year' / 'assessment year' terms.
personal.publisher: Indian Economic Service (Ministry of Finance) — Arthapedia
personal.quote: India’s financial year runs from 1st April to 31st March of next year.
personal.secondaryQuote: A 'Tax year' is a period of twelve months contained in a financial year. It replaces the term 'previous year' used in the Income Tax Act, 1961. The concept of "Tax Year " is applicable from 01 April 2026, i.e., for income earned during FY 2026 -27 onwards and this will be referred to as Tax Year 2026-27 under the Income Tax Act ,2025. [...] The 1961 Act stands repealed on the 01.04.2026 .
personal.licence: No licence statement found on the page (Government of India site).
personal.verification: ies.gov.in and incometax.gov.in (e-filing portal help, "Objective and scope of the New Act") fetched 2026-10-04. incometaxindia.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in answer 403 to automated fetches, so the statute text itself was not read.

us.zoneName: daylight saving time (e.g. EDT, UTC−4 for the Eastern zone)
us.ruleText: Clocks go forward one hour at 02:00 local time on the second Sunday in March and back one hour at 02:00 local time on the first Sunday in November, in every zone of a State that has not exempted itself.
us.exemptionsNote: The statute lets a State lying entirely within one time zone exempt itself; which States and territories have done so is not recorded here.

statute.publisher: 15 U.S.C. § 260a(a) (Uniform Time Act 1966 as amended by the Energy Policy Act of 2005) — U.S. Government Publishing Office
statute.quote: During the period commencing at 2 o'clock antemeridian on the second Sunday of March of each year and ending at 2 o'clock antemeridian on the first Sunday of November of each year, the standard time of each zone established by sections 261 to 264 of this title, as modified by section 265 of this title, shall be advanced one hour [...] however, (1) any State that lies entirely within one time zone may by law exempt itself from
statute.licence: Work of the United States Government — public domain (17 U.S.C. § 105)

au.name: Australia
au.zoneName: e.g. Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), UTC+11
au.ruleText: In the observing states and territories daylight saving begins at 02:00 standard time on the first Sunday in October and ends at 03:00 daylight time on the first Sunday in April (southern-hemisphere summer, so a period starting in one year ends in the next).

2026.note: southern hemisphere: the summer-time period that begins 2026-10-04 ends on the first Sunday in April 2027

2027.note: southern hemisphere: the summer-time period that begins 2027-10-03 ends on the first Sunday in April 2028

2028.note: southern hemisphere: the summer-time period that begins 2028-10-01 ends on the first Sunday in April 2029

statute.publisher: NSW Department of Communities and Justice (the department administering the Standard Time Act 1987 (NSW))
statute.quote: Each year, daylight saving begins at 2am on the first Sunday in October and ends at 3am on the first Sunday in April. Note that Lord Howe Island is an exception (clocks are put forward and back by 30 minutes). [...] NSW, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania, the Australian Capital Territory and Norfolk Island all observe the same period of daylight saving.

br.name: Brazil
br.ruleText: Brazil has had no daylight saving time since 2019: Decreto nº 9.772 of 26 April 2019 revoked the horário de verão.

statute.publisher: Presidência da República — Decreto nº 9.772, de 26 de abril de 2019
